description: Mutation sweep over the simulator kernel -- the pricing arithmetic every cost figure in this project rests on. B15L, B15M, B16D and the B19 preregistrations all call price_entry, price_exit and curve_fees directly rather than reimplementing them, so a guard here that no test can distinguish from its absence would make every downstream cost figure unverified.

mutants.name: protocol fee rounds down instead of up
creator fee rounds down instead of up
cashback rounds down instead of up
buyback is CHARGED as well as reported
creator fee dropped from the charged total
buyback rounds up instead of down
an exit may draw more than the curve holds
an entry may take more tokens than the curve holds
the reserve check made inclusive
a completed curve may be priced on entry
a non-native quote mint is accepted
mayhem mode is accepted
non-positive virtual reserves accepted
a sell is accepted as an entry
a zero-quote entry is accepted
an entry acquiring zero tokens is accepted
an exit may precede its entry
the causality check made exclusive of equality
a missing cost policy field is defaulted
a fee rate above 100 percent is accepted
a negative or float quantity is accepted
mutants.old: if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0:

mutants.name: failed attempts cost nothing

expected_survivors_note: None expected. Rounding direction, the buyback-is-reported-not-charged rule and the reserve solvency checks are the three places where a silent change would move every priced cell in the same direction.
